scenario: An international culinary contest invites chefs if they have either exceptional plating or exceptional flavor balance. A 10% wildcard also invites chefs with neither trait. Judges think plating and flavor are negatively related among invitees.

data.description: Invitation depends on either of two strengths plus a wildcard.

question: Among invited chefs, compute (a) P(plating | flavor, selected), and (b) P(plating | not flavor, selected). Is the negative association real or selection-induced?

ground_truth.explanation: The traits are independent in the population; the invitation rule induces the negative association.

naive_answer: Invitees with strong flavor seem less likely to have strong plating, so the traits likely conflict.
naive_trap: Conditioning on invitation creates a collider.
